newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air Liberte administrator has no Virgin bid.
newsitem.headline: Air Liberte administrator has no Virgin bid.

text.p: The court-appointed administrator of insolvent French airline Air Liberte said on Thursday that he had not received any offers from Richard Branson's Virgin Express to counter a 780 million franc bid by British Airways Plc and bank Rivaud.
"I have never seen any bid by Virgin so I do not see how they can increase a bid," Maitre Baronnie told Reuters by telephone.
He was reacting on a statement by Virgin Express chief executive officer Jonathan Ornstein who said in Brussels his company would raise its bid for the ailing French carrier.
Air Liberte administrator has no Virgin bid
Ornstein declined to give any figures for the bid, which still had to be submitted. "We're still formulating a plan...(we still have) a couple of days," he said, speaking by telephone.

Baronnie said he believed Virgin had been preparing to bid for some Air Liberte assets but not to offer to buy and run the airline. He said he doubted Virgin could put together an offer that would be more acceptable than the BA/Rivaud deal.
"I really doubt that there can be a bid better than BA/Rivaud, which takes on the debts, safeguards jobs and continues the company," he said.
At the Creteil commercial court, sources said there had been no new development in the Air Liberte case.
On Friday, the president of the court will chair a meeting to discuss the BA/Rivaud offer and a meeting with Air Liberte creditors has to be called within a month.
"Strictly theoretically, a new bid could be made just up to the moment that the creditors meet and accept the offer on the table. In the end the creditors decide," Baronnie said.

BA/Rivaud are offering Air Liberte creditors either 20 percent of the outstanding debt at once or full payment over 10 years. Air Liberte went into administration on September 26 with debts of 1.5 billion francs ($291.8 million). ($ = 5.14 French Francs)
